description: The NPBench and Pythran entry functions Zinnia accepts that have an audited SP1/RISC Zero port: the zkVM performance comparison beyond DS-1000. Written by datasets/tools/npbench_pythran_perf.py; do not edit.

rules.status_order: The author RQ1 acceptance expansion in rq1_selection_overrides takes precedence; otherwise: A case gets the first status whose rule applies, in this order: not_in_acceptance_results, zinnia_rejects, no_zkvm_port, port_excluded, port_not_audited, perf.
rules.not_in_acceptance_results: The acceptance results given to the generator have no row for the entry function.
rules.zinnia_rejects: The acceptance run did not accept the entry function with outputs equal to NumPy's (its outcome and construct are in the reason).
rules.no_zkvm_port: The program's zkvm.rs has no module for the function, or the zkVM crates do not register it (run baselines/zkvm_common/sync_cases.py).
rules.port_excluded: The port audit excludes the port (reason in the audit record).
rules.port_not_audited: The port audit does not cover the current zkvm.rs (new entry, or the file changed since the audit): review it and update the audit record.
rules.perf: Measured: Zinnia accepts the function, and its SP1/RISC Zero port is audited.
rules.sizes: Shapes and scalar values are the acceptance fixture's (acceptance.json `sizing`: every dimension and size scalar at most 16); keys come from input A, proofs from input B.
rules.mutated_outputs: A function that returns None outputs the array arguments it writes, in parameter order (the port's `// outputs: mutated` line, checked against NumPy on inputs A and B).
rules.data_movement_only: true when the outputs depend on private inputs only by copying them; such cases stay perf and are reported apart.
